articles.headline: Broncos' Jonathon Cooper off commissioner exempt list, could return Week 7
articles.description: Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper was removed from the commissioner exempt list Friday, meaning he's available to play in Week 7. Cooper, who was arrested twice in a seven-day span in June on domestic violence charges, has been on the list since Aug. 30.
articles.body:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- NFL commissioner Roger Goodell removed Denver Broncos outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper from the league's exempt list Friday.

Cooper, who was unable to practice or play in games while he was on the list, will now be available to play in the Broncos' Week 7 road game against the Arizona Cardinals.

Cooper, who was arrested twice in a seven-day span in June on domestic violence charges, has been on the exempt list since Aug. 30.

Cooper was in Douglas County (Colorado) court last week for a motions hearing and has a March 2-4 trial scheduled in his case, as well as a pretrial hearing scheduled for Feb. 19 . In a statement Friday, the NFL said its review of Cooper's case "remains ongoing and is not affected by this change to Cooper's roster status.''

It means Cooper could still face league discipline at a later date under the NFL's personal conduct policy.

The Broncos will get a one-week roster exemption for Cooper, who can now return to practice. He could then be added to the 53-man roster at any point over the next week and play Oct. 25 against the Cardinals.

He had been able to attend meetings and other team functions, including weight room and conditioning work, when he was on the exempt list.

The exempt list is designed to remove a player from participation in games and practices while potential violations of the NFL's personal conduct policy are reviewed. Cooper has been paid while on the list.

His time on the exempt list -- the first six weeks of the regular season -- would count toward any league-mandated suspension in the future. He would, however, if suspended, have to return the weekly game checks he has received because suspensions from the personal conduct policy are without pay.

Cooper had practiced throughout training camp.

Cooper faces a felony charge of second-degree assault by strangulation and three misdemeanors, including violating a protection order, after he was arrested June 4 and then again June 11 after incidents involving his girlfriend. 

The felony charge stemmed from the first arrest after the results of a forensic examination of Cooper's girlfriend by a nurse.

The affidavit that was included in the police investigation into Cooper's first arrest included the report from the medical exam of Cooper's girlfriend. In it, a nurse wrote that the woman experienced a physical injury from being choked that led to a "substantial risk of death" or substantial risk of injury, including the possibility of traumatic brain injury.

Broncos coach Sean Payton has consistently deferred to the NFL's investigation and the legal process when he has discussed the team's approach with the sixth-year linebacker. Payton said that the Broncos set guidelines for Cooper after the arrest and that that has included therapy.

Cooper was a seventh-round pick in the 2021 draft and has 31.5 sacks in 81 career games with the Broncos, including eight sacks last season. He has started every game in each of the past three seaso

articles.headline: Eagles' Saquon Barkley ruled out; DeVonta Smith to return
articles.description: Eagles RB Saquon Barkley has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Panthers with a hamstring injury, but it appears WR DeVonta Smith will return.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- Eagles running back Saquon Barkley has been ruled out for Sunday's home game against the Carolina Panthers with a hamstring injury, but it appears receiver DeVonta Smith will make his return to the lineup.

Smith does not carry an injury designation after missing the previous two games with a hamstring injury.

"I'm good," Smith said when asked about the injury after practice Friday, adding that whether he plays is "up to the doctors."

With Barkley, Will Shipley and Tank Bigsby all ruled out, Dameon Pierce is in line to get the bulk of the carries out of the backfield.

Barkley exited early in the first quarter of the Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams and has been sidelined since. Shipley was placed on injured reserve Friday with a foot injury, joining Bigsby (abdomen).

Tanner McKee, meanwhile, is slated to start in place of quarterback Jalen Hurts, who was ruled out Thursday due to a superficial blood clot in his calf.

Edge rusher Jonathan Greenard said he plans to test his ankle pregame, as he did in London before being ruled out against the Jaguars, though he carries no designation. Fellow edge rushers Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) and AJ Epenesa (back) and safety Michael Carter (abdomen) have been ruled out.

Linemen Landon Dickerson and Drew Kendall are questionable with knee injuries.

articles.headline: Packers' Josh Jacobs eligible to return next week amid probe
articles.description: Packers RB Josh Jacobs will be removed from the commissioner exempt list Monday, the league announced, making him eligible to practice and play next week.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Packers running back Josh Jacobs will be removed from the commissioner exempt list Monday, the league announced, making him eligible to practice and play next week.

The league's investigation into Jacobs under the personal conduct policy remains ongoing, however, leaving open the possibility that he could still be suspended.

When he comes off the list next week, Jacobs will have missed the first six games of the season, and those games would count toward any suspension. However, if Jacobs ends up getting suspended for more than six games, he would have to miss additional games to make up the difference.

After playing the Cowboys this Sunday at Lambeau Field, the Packers will visit the Lions on Oct. 25. 

"Josh has dedicated the last several months to bettering himself, and he accepts responsibility for his actions," Jacobs' attorneys, Clarence F. Duchac III, David Z. Chesnoff and Richard A. Schonfeld, said in a statement. "He is excited to get back to work and on the field with his teammates. Josh is grateful for the support he is receiving from his teammates, coaches, the Packers organization, and the greatest fans in the world."

Jacobs was placed on the commissioner exempt list Aug. 30 while the NFL continued to gather information about the May 23 incident with a woman at his home near Green Bay.

Jacobs pleaded no contest Sept. 10 to charges of battery and criminal destruction of property. He was convicted of battery and fined $1,000 and agreed to a deferred judgment agreement on a charge of damage to property.

The woman did not speak with the NFL upon request due to privacy concerns, one of her attorneys, Amir Tahmassebi, said. Jacobs, meanwhile, did speak to the league, a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.

Part of the reason the league has not closed its investigation is because it has not seen the surveillance video from Jacobs' home that was noted in the criminal report. The video showed the portion of the incident that occurred in Jacobs' garage but not from inside the house.

On Sept. 24, Brown County (Wisconsin) Circuit Court judge Marc A. Hammer lifted a temporary seal of the records and turned the decision whether to release part or all of the records over to the Hobart/Lawrence (Wisconsin) police department.

On Tuesday, the police department announced it would release some records but did not say whether the surveillance video was part of the documents it deemed available for public consumption. However, that release would be delayed pending appeals from the parties involved.

On Wednesday, both Jacobs and the victim in the case filed suit to block the release of evidence and have it permanently sealed.

articles.headline: Decked-out, diehard Jaguars fans swarm London for pub takeover
articles.description: Jaguars fans roll deep in the United Kingdom, and the fandom showed up big at London's briefly renamed ''Tealwood'' pub Thursday night.
articles.body:
LONDON -- For three hours Thursday night, the Greenwood sports pub and kitchen on Victoria Street in Central London ceased to exist. In its place: Tealwood.

An apt renaming, as Greenwood was hosting one of three pub takeover events sponsored by the Jacksonville Jaguars' U.K. branch for Jaguars fans who live in the United Kingdom or made the trip to London for the team's annual home game at Wembley Stadium this Sunday.

There will be another Friday night and Saturday afternoon, and there was one the previous Friday night in advance of the Jaguars' home game at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last week, which they won 19-17 on Cam Little's 57-yard field goal as time expired.

Those events are part of the NFL franchise's movement to continue to build its international fanbase, a push that began back in 2013 when the team played the first of what is now 15 games in London. The Jaguars also have their own U.K. fan club (Union Jax), have been heavily involved in helping to build interest in flag football with clinics, have appearances with current and former players throughout the year, run a year-round junior cheerleading program and send hundreds of students annually to the London games as part of a Reward Rows program.

"Even if you knew nothing about the NFL, you were like, 'Oh, but the Jags are our team,'" said Phoebe Schecter, a former Buffalo Bills coaching intern, one of the first members of the Great Britain national American football team and now an NFL analyst for Sky Sports. "And so I think there's always going to be that really great association.

"The Jags really do have a presence [in the U.K.], and the fans are truly bought in, and you get superfans. I mean, something as silly as somebody's on social, it's like a Mr. and Mrs. Jaxson de Ville, but they're superfans here in the U.K. and they're bought into the costumes and this whole persona. It's who they are. And you see that in the States, and now that's kind of creeping in over here in a great way."

Jamie Phillips and Francis Sweeney are two of those fans. Sweeney -- decked out in an oversized Jaguars hat, jersey and jacket and carrying a Jags-themed wrestling belt over his shoulder -- has attended the team's games in London for the past five years. He's not the only Jags fan in his family, though.

"My wife doesn't like any sports, and she's obsessed with the Jaguars," he said.

Phillips, who was at Thursday night's pub takeover, wore a Jaguars mascot fuzzy hat on the 59-degree day at the Jaguars' practice at The Grove resort, the team's headquarters since it arrived Oct. 9. He was the team's 2024 nominee for the NFL's International Fan of the Year and has been a Jaguars fan for 15 years.

That began two years before the Jaguars started making annual trips overseas, but Phillips latched on to the franchise even though it had just three winning seasons since the 2000s began.

"I want to take after the underdog as most Brits do," he said. "A bit of an obsession, really, is what it's become

articles.headline: Fantasy football 12-team Knockout league rankings: The 168 players to draft
articles.description: Rankings for knockout leagues, where the lowest-scoring team is eliminated and the last team standing wins.
articles.body:
Tristan H. Cockcroft's 2026 fantasy football Knockout league rankings will be updated throughout the season to reflect the latest news, trends and opinions. Use them to inform your own rankings, or as a guide to draft your team. Sign up for your team for free.

Knockout leagues are our newest offering for 2026, challenging fantasy football managers to avoid being the last-place scorer in any given week, with the final team standing winning the championship. For those new to the format, here's a strategy primer to help you fine-tune your game.

The rankings below will differ slightly from our standard offering in that Knockout leagues begin with 18 teams, creating more demand at thinner positions such as quarterback and tight end. Additionally, week-over-week consistency carries additional weight, players with injury or other availability concerns are less desirable, and later-year bye weeks can prove advantageous. A standard 18-team knockout league comprises 14 slots including a kicker and a defense, so the rankings began 252 deep at season's start, and are now 168 deep (12 teams times 14 players) for leagues drafting to begin in Week 7, to take you from the first overall selection through to the final pick of the draft.

Remember that if you want to start a league that plays this week your draft must be completed by the time players lock for Thursday Night Football, otherwise your league will begin play the following week.  A 12-team league lets you eliminate 11 players through Week 17, leaving only the winner standing.

articles.headline: Bears' Caleb Williams questionable after 3 days of practice
articles.description: The quarterback said there are several hurdles to clear before he would be able to face the Falcons on Sunday.
articles.body:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- Quarterback Caleb Williams was officially listed as questionable on the Chicago Bears' final injury report ahead of their Week 6 game at the Atlanta Falcons (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET, Fox).

Williams was a full participant during the Bears' Wednesday walk-through and practice sessions Thursday and Friday. The quarterback said he had to go through "a bunch of medical protocols" before being cleared by team trainers, which could happen before the team leaves for Atlanta.

"I'm hopeful we'll have more clarity at the end of the day today," Bears coach Ben Johnson said Friday. "He looked good [Thursday] for one practice, but we've got to be able to stack a few back-to-back. He got some good work in on Wednesday, even though we walked through, he went through his own throwing session beforehand. Part of the plan, and he's on track right now."

Williams missed three straight games while recovering from a hamstring injury sustained during the fourth quarter of a Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. On Thursday, he took issue with the reporting around his injury, for which he claimed that "nothing that has come out that has been right about what it is and what it has been."

Johnson did not sense that his quarterback was frustrated with anything other than not being able to play.

"I, honestly, I didn't feel any frustration from him," Johnson said. "He was in this little bit of a no-man's land, 'Hey, what do I what do with myself? I've never been in this situation. I've never been in the training room this much. I've never been second or third fiddle in the quarterback room ever in my life.' Just like, 'I just need a little guidance on how I can best help and serve.'

"He's a captain, he wants to do that desperately. 'How can I help us win in this different setting?' I don't know that I felt frustration, other than an eagerness to get back out there and help the guys on the field."

While Williams' status is questionable, the Bears will be without running back Kyle Monangai for a second straight game. Monangai did not practice this week while recovering from thumb and toe injuries, the latter of which he visited a specialist for last week.

"It wasn't one of those things we felt like we needed to put him on IR for," Johnson said. "So, it's still week-to-week, and as far as I know he's trending in the right direction."

Chicago will also be down three starters on defense, with defensive end Montez Sweat's two-game suspension for violating the PED policy and injuries that are sidelining linebacker T.J. Edwards (hamstring) and Dayo Odeyingbo (quad) in Week 6.

articles.headline: Mikel Arteta told Arsenal job cuts will help club 'achieve success'
articles.description: Mikel Arteta has been told Arsenal's redundancies will help the club "achieve the success we want to create" after it emerged the Premier League champions are set to cut 60 jobs.
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta has been told Arsenal's redundancies will help the club "achieve the success we want to create" after it emerged the Premier League champions are set to cut 60 jobs.

Chief executive Richard Garlick informed staff this week that Arsenal's workforce will be reduced across a number of departments -- although the playing and coaching staff in the men's and women's teams will be unaffected.

- Arteta defends Gyökeres after goalless start to season

- Merino lucky 'to be alive' after Dortmund bus attack

- Forest sweating on Gibbs-White fitness vs. Arsenal

The cuts are set to impact up to 7% of the club's 871 permanent staff.

Arteta was last week rewarded with a new four-year deal, worth as much as £20 million ($27m) a season, after he oversaw Arsenal's first Premier League title since 2004.

Arsenal's turnover for the 2024-25 season was a record £691m ($920m).

"First, this question is not for me," Arteta said on Friday when asked about the expected job losses in his news conference ahead of Sunday's league match against Nottingham Forest.

"It was explained to me about the exercise, and the analysis that has been done across the club, and with the intention always to evolve to improve.

"Some decisions have to be taken to put people in the right roles, and keep investing, to achieve what we want to achieve the success that we want to create. That has been explained.

"Obviously, I am not the right person to answer to that question. That's for sure. And hopefully everybody will respect that."

Arteta did not take any further questions on the topic at the request of the club.

The 44-year-old Spaniard also confirmed that the club will retake Arsenal's official squad photo following William Saliba's omission.

The France international, who last season played an integral role in the club winning the league title, was conspicuous by his absence from the picture which was released on Thursday.

He is currently sidelined with a back problem, and Arsenal said he was not available because of a "medical appointment."

"We have tried to do that picture three times already," explained Arteta on Friday. "We had to cancel it at the last minute for different reasons.

"We have some commercial obligations, and we had people that flew over because of that. We decided to do that picture at least.

"We'll have another picture with the whole family. Hopefully we can get them all together at some point. He [Saliba] knows how loved he is. He's completely fine about it."

Saliba has not played since the World Cup but there is an outside chance he could be available before the international break next month.

Martín Zubimendi is in contention to face Forest despite sustaining an ankle injury in training directly after Arsenal's win over Leeds at the Emirates Stadium last weekend. Piero Hincapié, who also suffered an ankle problem during the post-match session, will not feature.

articles.headline: NBA tells sportsbooks to stop certain bets, restrict parlays
articles.description: The NBA is prohibiting certain bets this season, including a player prop parlay used in recent scandals, according to a league memo to sportsbook partners.
articles.headlineJa: NBA、ブックメーカーに対し特定の賭けの停止とパーレイの制限を指示
articles.descriptionJa: NBAがブックメーカーのパートナーに送ったメモによると、最近のスキャンダルで用いられたプレイヤープロップのパーレイを含む、特定の賭けが今シーズンは禁止される。
articles.body:
The NBA is prohibiting certain types of bets this season, including a player prop parlay used by gamblers in recent betting scandals, according to a league memo distributed to sportsbook partners Friday.

Bettors will not be able to include the under on the same player's statistics in parlays, in addition to other betting markets the league considers problematic, according to the memo, which was obtained by ESPN.

The NBA also directed its authorized gambling operators, including DraftKings and FanDuel, not to offer bets on the winner of the opening tip, players to miss specific shots and under bets on players who are expected to play fewer than 12 minutes in a specific game.

"There's a balance between ensuring that we are removing problematic bet types but also ensuring that we don't just move activity into the illegal market," NBA executive vice president Scott Kaufman-Ross told ESPN. "And where we landed right now, we think, is the right balance of those two objectives."

The NBA has the authority to restrict what partner sportsbooks offer through its agreements. The NBA estimates its partner sportsbooks account for upward of 99% of the U.S. betting market.

"The legalized sports betting industry is built on a foundation of dialogue and collaboration with our league partners and the states in which we operate," a FanDuel spokesperson said in a statement to ESPN. "We remain unwavering in our commitment to building a legal and regulated market that roots out abuses by those who seek to undermine fair competition and damage the integrity of the games we love."

Parlay bets on a single player's unders appeared in the federal cases involving NBA players Jontay Porter and Terry Rozier.

Porter admitted in court that he intentionally removed himself from games early to benefit bettors while he was on a two-way contract with the Toronto Raptors during the 2023-24 season.

In the criminal complaint, federal prosecutors said one of the bettors charged in the scheme placed an $80,000 parlay on the under on Porter's assists, rebounds, points, 3-pointers, steals and blocks for a March 2024 game between the Raptors and Sacramento Kings that would pay approximately $1.1 million. Porter left the game after playing only three minutes.

Federal prosecutors allege bettors took a similar approach a year earlier with parlays involving the under on Rozier's stats in a March 2023 game between the Charlotte Hornets and New Orleans Pelicans. The veteran guard, who was with the Hornets at the time, left after playing approximately nine minutes. Rozier has pleaded not guilty and denied wrongdoing.

Kaufman-Ross said the Porter and Rozier cases were factors in the decision to prohibit such parlays that were described as "low likelihood, high payout bets" in the memo. Sportsbooks also will be prohibited from offering alternate lines on unders with larger payouts.

articles.headline: Buss siblings' filing challenges Jeanie's petition to oust them as trustees
articles.description: The legal jostling between five of the Buss siblings against their sister, Lakers acting governor Jeanie Buss, continued with an additional filing submitted to the Los Angeles Superior Court.
articles.headlineJa: バス家の兄弟、受託者解任を求めるジーニーの請願に対し申し立てで対抗
articles.descriptionJa: レイカーズの暫定オーナーを務める姉のジーニー・バスと、バス家の5人の兄弟との間で続く法的な争いが、ロサンゼルス高等裁判所へ提出された新たな申し立てによって継続している。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- The legal jostling between five of the Buss siblings against their sister, Lakers acting governor Jeanie Buss, continued Friday with an additional filing submitted to the Los Angeles Superior Court.

The 29-page document, reviewed by ESPN, was filed on behalf of Joey and Janie Buss in opposition to their sister and her previous petition seeking to remove them as co-trustees and void the siblings' 5-1 vote to sell the family's remaining stake in the team.

"This dispute turns on (1) who had the authority to decide whether the Trust would continue, (2) what event would terminate it, and (3) what the Trustee Respondents were required to do once that event occurred," Friday's filing says. "The Trust's text unambiguously answers each question."

The new filing not only argues Joey and Janie's right to hold the vote to sell and highlights language in the trust that states a sale requires a two-thirds majority by the siblings, which they exceeded, but it also challenges the breadth of Jeanie's rights as a co-trustee and acting governor.

The filing follows a 36-page opposition submitted to the court Oct. 7 by all five siblings -- Jimmy, Johnny and Jesse included -- that argued their right to terminate the family trust and sell their remaining 17.82% of the team to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger's ownership group after the pair agreed to purchase the Lakers from Mark Walter at a $12.5 billion valuation.

Both filings come in response to Jeanie, through her lawyer Adam Streisand, submitting a 97-page petition to the court in August aimed to block the sale of the family's stake in the team to Kushner and Iger, who, sources told ESPN, are expected to take control of the franchise following an NBA board of governors vote in November.

Friday's filing contends that a 2017 court decision that instructed the trustees to take "whatever actions are reasonably available" to have Jeanie appointed as the controlling owner while the family trust holds Lakers stock became moot once a vote was held to terminate the trust to facilitate a sale.

"It does not require the Trust to remain in existence for Jeanie's lifetime ... or require the Trust to maintain any minimum ownership percentage," the filing states.

The NBA requires a controlling owner to maintain a 15% stake in a team to operate in that position, though Friday's filing states that the 15% figure is not included anywhere in the original trust or in the 2017 order.

The new filing also contends that while the family trust barred any sale of Lakers stock during Dr. Jerry Buss' lifetime without his consent, it contains no comparable restriction connected to Jeanie. Furthermore, Friday's filing argues that a sale to Kushner and Iger will maximize value of the trust's 185.59 shares of the Lakers for all the beneficiaries, including Jeanie.

articles.headline: Spanish team challenging Thunder rookie Aday Mara's NBA eligibility
articles.description: A Spanish basketball team is challenging Thunder rookie Aday Mara's eligibility to play in the NBA this season, saying he is still under contract with the club.
articles.headlineJa: スペインのチーム、サンダーの新人アダイ・マラのNBA出場資格に異議を唱える
articles.descriptionJa: スペインのバスケットボールチームが、サンダーの新人のアダイ・マラは依然としてクラブと契約中であるとして、今シーズンのNBA出場資格に異議を唱えている。
articles.body:
Spanish club Basket Zaragoza is challenging Oklahoma City Thunder rookie lottery pick Aday Mara's eligibility to play in the NBA this season, stating that he remains under contract with the team for the 2026-27 season, a contention disputed by the Thunder.

In a statement released Friday, Basket Zaragoza said it has not received an official request from the Thunder for Mara's international transfer and would formally oppose the transfer if a request is made.

"Aday last played three years of NCAA college basketball and therefore, as advised by the NBA, no clearance from the Spanish team is required for him to play in the NBA," a Thunder spokesperson said Friday.

Basket Zaragoza said its position was formally communicated to FIBA, the Spanish Basketball Federation, the NBA and the Thunder after Oklahoma City selected Mara with the No. 12 pick in June's draft.

Mara, a native of Zaragoza, left the club in 2023 to go to UCLA. However, FIBA regulations do not require an official international transfer for NCAA participation, and Basket Zaragoza's stance is that Mara's contract with the club was not terminated during his college tenure. After two seasons at UCLA, the 7-foot-3 Mara transferred to Michigan, where he started on last season's national championship team before entering the draft.

The 21-year-old Mara had an outstanding preseason for Oklahoma City, averaging 13.4 points, 7.6 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 2.4 blocks while shooting 78.8% from the floor in 23.3 minutes per game. He is projected to be part of a deep center rotation for the Thunder, who use 7-footers Isaiah Hartenstein and Chet Holmgren in the starting lineup and bring Jaylin Williams off the bench.

articles.headline: Lisandro Martínez's Man United comments 'not that far off' but should not have been made - Peter Schmeichel
articles.description: Former Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel has said he believes Lisandro Martínez's criticism of the club's hierarchy is "not that far off."
articles.headlineJa: リサンドロ・マルティネスのマンUに関する発言は「的外れではない」が、すべきではなかった ― ピーター・シュマイケル
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドの元ゴールキーパー、ピーター・シュマイケルは、リサンドロ・マルティネスによるクラブ幹部への批判は「決して的外れではない」との見解を示した。
articles.body:
Former Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel has said he believes Lisandro Martínez's criticism of the club's hierarchy is "not that far off" but added he would not have liked hearing a teammate sound off in public.

Schmeichel was criticised for his handling of a post-match interview with Martínez in the aftermath of Tuesday night's 2-0 Champions League loss to Atlético Madrid, when the Argentina defender turned his fire on the club's hierarchy and named director of football Jason Wilcox as one of those from whom he "expects more."

Martínez spoke first to Amazon Prime's Gabriel Clarke before Schmeichel interviewed him for U.S. broadcaster CBS, with the defender repeating many of his criticisms while Schmeichel appeared to be trying to move Martínez on from the topic.

On Thursday Martínez issued a public apology for his comments and United said the matter was considered closed after the 28-year-old met with manager Michael Carrick, Wilcox and the club's hierarchy.

But inevitably the issue dominated Carrick's news conference on Friday with the substance of Martínez's comments still being debated.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, Schmeichel said: "I would not like any teammate ever to go out and talk like that. Unless it was Bryan Robson... No, I wouldn't. I absolutely wouldn't like that.

"In the dressing rooms I was in, you were accountable. It just didn't happen very often that somebody stepped out of line, and of course we had a manager [Sir Alex Ferguson] who would not allow you to step out of line. He would react to that straight away...

"It's not that I completely disagree with what [Martínez] says. That's the other thing."

- Man United 'a circus' amid Lisandro Martínez rant - Roy Keane

Schmeichel then added: "Without going into too much detail about what Martínez said, some of the things he said are not far off.

"Look at the promising teams: Manchester City a long time ago, Arsenal for the past six years, Liverpool under Jürgen Klopp -- what did they do that suddenly changed the dynamics and changed their fortunes? They started at the back.

"They got in a goalkeeper, back four, a centre midfield player. They built that foundation, made it solid, and then they started to bring the creative players in. They've all done it... Built from the back. We've done the opposite, built from the front."

articles.headline: Inter Milan rocked as captain Lautaro Martínez set to miss 7 games
articles.description: Inter Milan captain Lautaro Martínez will likely miss his team's next seven matches, including the derby against city rival AC Milan, with a hamstring injury.
articles.body:
Inter Milan captain Lautaro Martínez will likely miss his team's next seven matches, including the derby against city rivals AC Milan, with a hamstring injury.

Martínez played the whole of Tuesday's Champions League match against Club Brugge and scored two goals in the 4-3 defeat. But medical tests on Thursday revealed a strain in his left hamstring.

- Lautaro Martínez: World Cup goal against England 'one of the most important in Argentina history'

"He will be out for a while," Inter coach Cristian Chivu said on Friday. "I'm not a doctor. I've been given a recovery timeframe, and he'll probably be back after the international break."

Martínez will certainly miss Saturday's trip to Bologna and Wednesday's Champions League match against Shakhtar Donetsk. Inter then play Fiorentina and Venezia before the derby against Milan on Oct. 31.

They also face Feyenoord and Como before the international break. Inter's first match back is at Atalanta on Nov. 22.

Martínez has six goals in seven matches across the Champions League and Serie A this season. He was Serie A's top goalscorer last season with 17 -- the second time he's won that award.

Martínez also scored twice for Argentina -- against Bolivia and Burkina Faso -- in the recent international window.

Argentina on Friday announced that they will take part in two friendlies in November -- against Uruguay on Nov. 13 in Buenos Aires and versus Costa Rica on Nov. 17 in Cordoba.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: David Moyes on new contract talks at Everton: 'Bit of a lull'
articles.description: David Moyes has said discussions over a new contract at the Hill Dickinson Stadium have gone quiet following news that Everton could be up for sale.
articles.body:
David Moyes has said discussions over a new contract at the Hill Dickinson Stadium have gone quiet following the news that Everton could be up for sale.

Everton's owners -- The Friedkin Group -- announced last week they were exploring the possibility of selling their controlling interest in the Merseyside outfit.

Toffees manager Moyes is in the final year of his deal and the Scot is not expecting imminent developments on fresh terms.

"There's been plenty of talks happening through the summer but maybe with the way things have gone at the moment, there's maybe been a bit of a lull, trying to get things in order," Moyes said at a news conference.

"But like I've said many times, it's not the most important thing for me. I just want to keep trying to drive Everton on and build them up, and see if we can continue to improve."

- Everton put up for sale by Friedkin Group

- 777 exec Wander, who led Everton bid, guilty of fraud; to repay $500M

Everton host Chelsea in the Premier League on Saturday.

Moyes said: "Anytime I've played Chelsea, it's always been a good game. It was always tough.

"But we will do our best. We're in quite a good place. We've been playing well ourselves."

articles.headline: Bucks adjust home opener to avoid World Series time conflict
articles.description: The Bucks are going to have an afternoon tipoff for their Oct. 23 home opener with the Bulls to avoid a direct conflict with Game 1 of the World Series.
articles.body:
MILWAUKEE -- The Milwaukee Bucks are going to have an afternoon tipoff for their Oct. 23 home opener with the Chicago Bulls to avoid a direct conflict with Game 1 of the World Series, which is taking place in Milwaukee that evening.

The Bucks announced Friday that their home opener would take place at 3 p.m. CT rather than 7 p.m. Bucks officials said they worked with the NBA office to make the schedule change possible.

The Milwaukee Brewers will host the Cleveland Guardians or Tampa Bay Rays in Game 1 of the World Series that night. The Brewers clinched their first World Series berth since 1982 on Thursday.

"The Brewers' return to the World Series for the first time in 44 years is a special moment for Milwaukee and sports fans across Wisconsin," the Bucks said in a statement. "Congratulations to the Brewers and the entire organization on this tremendous achievement, and we'll be cheering them on as they begin their World Series run. The Bucks are proud to move our home opener to 3 p.m. in recognition of this historic occasion and thank the NBA for making this schedule change possible."

The Bucks are opening their season Wednesday at Washington.

The Bucks also have another potential World Series scheduling issue. They're scheduled to host the Cleveland Cavaliers the night of Oct. 31, which is when Game 7 would take place in Milwaukee if the World Series goes the distance.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look on the court in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

Oct. 16

Marks: A busy weekend of transaction expected

The last weekend of the offseason is expected to bring a flurry of transactions.

Starting on Saturday Oct. 17, teams will need to decide on players signed to non-guaranteed contracts. If a player is on the roster past 5 p.m. ET, teams will begin incurring a per day salary charge.

For example, the New York Knicks would be charged $17,622 per day against the cap if James Wiseman is not waived by Saturday. However, despite a mandate to remain under the second apron, New York is allowed to keep Wiseman and Bruce Brown to start the season.

The deadline for rookie extensions is Monday by 6 p.m. ET.

Since the start of the offseason, five players -- Victor Wembanyama, Amen and Ausar Thompson, Keyonte George and Brandin Podziemski -- have signed rookie extensions. The 2023 rookie class of extended players are below the per year average of 11 players we have seen since 2023.

Some of the notable names to watch include Brandon Miller and Cason Wallace. Keep in mind that out of the 34 players who signed rookie extensions in the prior three seasons, 17 came on the last day of eligibility.

The rookie extension deadline is not the only date teams are paying attention to, however. Oct. 19 is also the deadline to extend veterans who have two years left on their contract -- not including an option year -- and the last day to reduce rosters to 15 players on standard contracts. -- Bobby Marks

articles.headline: Alone on a fantasy basketball island: 'One player I feel differently about'
articles.description: The fantasy basketball crew identifies one player they feel differently about than seemingly everyone else.
articles.body:
With how closely fantasy basketball managers and analysts are watching every player and roster role, it's easy get lost in all of the information available. But beyond that, everyone has that one opinion they may be a little stubborn on. 

You know, that one player you are certain will break out to join the league's elite. Or maybe a player everyone around is high on, but you're feeling the "meh."

That's why we asked our fantasy basketball experts André Snellings, Eric Moody, Eric Karabell, Jim McCormick, Michael F. Florio and Steve Alexander to identify a player they feel differently about for this season and their bold prediction why.

See more:  Sign up | Rankings | Projections | Mock Draft Lobby 

Draft guide | Cheat sheet | Which league is right for you? 

Fred VanVleet is a steal at his current spot

VanVleet going outside the top 100 picks is one of the easiest clicks of the draft button for me. I understand that he missed last season, but any risk is already baked into his ADP. He's back as the starting point guard for a very talented Rockets team. VanVleet is a season removed from averaging eight assists per game. He averaged over 17 fantasy PPG in five of his last six seasons. You can take Desmond Bane in the top 50 picks, or wait and get similar production with VanVleet. -- Florio

LaMelo Ball could have the best season of his career

I am higher than most on LaMelo Ball. Ball played in 72 games last season, his most since the 2021-22 campaign, but he also played a career-low 28.0 MPG with associated lesser volume. But in the three previous, injury-shortened seasons, Ball averaged much higher volume at 24.1 PPG, 7.9 APG and 5.5 RPG. With Ball moving to the Timberwolves, a team that has desperately needed a playmaker, and playing as one of two elite offensive options next to Anthony Edwards, I could see Ball having the best season of his career. I remember Ball was a preseason top-10 player entering the 2022-23 campaign before the ankle injuries slowed him down, and if he stays healthy I could see him return to that range this season. -- Snellings

Jaren Jackson Jr.'s days as a top-100 option could be over

After years of investing in JJJ, I am out, especially in points formats. Jackson blocks shots and shoots well, but we cannot count on Jackson averaging 20 PPG again, and he has never been much of a rebounder or passer, routinely piling on more turnovers than assists. Considering his size and talent, there is no reason for Jackson to average fewer than eight RPG. He's not even getting six RPG! Darryn Peterson and Ace Bailey are Utah's future. Jackson's role may be reduced even further, enough that he may no longer be a top-100 fantasy option at all. -- Karabell
